flags: The 236-mile tourism itinerary and the 184.5-mile canal are different routes. Material’s mapped mileage is 228.2; the overview uses the tourism itinerary length. Its final strip-mile values restart near Travilah; order follows the west-to-east itinerary rather than sorting those reset values.
Dropped the current blanket claim that the river is on one hand and the towpath never far off: the cache does not establish continuous roadside proximity.

Corrected the current exact six-million-brick claim to more than six million. Paw Paw’s dedicated article dates construction from 1836 to opening in 1850, with a six-year hiatus; the general canal article says almost twelve years. The draft uses the explicit dates and hiatus.
Williamsport’s canal-arrival dates disagree between the general canal and town articles (1834/1835); no arrival date is used.
The canal article gives both 605 feet of elevation change and 610 feet at Cumberland. The overview omits the elevation figure.

Boat rides at Williamsport and Great Falls are supported by the February 2026 tourism archive, but no separate site-operator confirmation is cached. The draft focuses on structures and history rather than promising rides.
Paw Paw’s cached access discussion includes old 2013 and 2017–2019 works. No present closure, reopening or unrestricted passage is inferred.
No road-building or byway designation-date history is cached; the overview tells the canal’s documented transport history and identifies the scenic byway through Maryland’s tourism office.

The current overview implies coal carriage continued to the 1924 flood. The canal article identifies the last known coal boat in November 1923 and only sand cargoes in 1924; the revision separates principal cargo from closure date.
